extraction.name: SciQ
extraction.description: A dataset of 13.7K multiple choice science exam questions generated by crowd workers.
extraction.creator: Johannes Welbl, Nelson F. Liu, Matt Gardner
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A two-step process where crowd workers first choose a passage and ask a question about it, and then another worker validates the question and produces three distractors aided by a model.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science study textbooks from online learning resources, including CK-12 and OpenStax.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rule-based document filter was used to classify individual sentences and accept paragraphs based on lexical, grammatical, pragmatical, and complexity rules.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Workers judged whether the question could appear in a school science exam, selected up to two of the six model-suggested distractors, and wrote at least one distractor themselves.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A qualitative evaluation was conducted where humans were asked to distinguish crowdsourced questions from original exam questions; they could only identify the real question 55% of the time.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowd workers with Master's status on Amazon Mechanical Turk.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: A random forest classifier trained to predict good answer distractors.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The multiple choice version does not include the passage. A small percentage of passages were from unreleasable texts, making the direct answer version slightly smaller.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing for reading comprehension and science QA models.

name.evidence: With this method we have assembled SciQ , a dataset of 13.7K multiple choice science exam questions.

description.evidence: With this method we have assembled SciQ , a dataset of 13.7K multiple choice science exam questions.

creator.evidence: Johannes Welbl Computer Science Department University College London... Nelson F. Liu Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering University of Washington... Matt Gardner Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The method is a two-step process: first we present a set of candidate passages to a crowd worker, letting the worker choose one of the passages and ask a question about it. Second, another worker takes the question and answer generated in the first step and produces three distractors, aided by a model trained to predict good answer distractors.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: we present a set of candidate passages to a crowd worker, letting the worker choose one of the passages and ask a question about it.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We chose science study textbooks as our base corpus because they are directly relevant and linguistically tailored towards a student audience. ... we compiled a list of 28 books from various online learning resources, including CK-12 and OpenStax

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We designed a rule-based document filter model into which individual paragraphs of the base corpus are fed. The system classifies individual sentences and accepts a paragraph if a minimum number of sentences is accepted. ... The final filter included lexical, grammatical, pragmatical and complexity based rules.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: The first instruction was to judge whether the question could appear in a school science exam... The second instruction was to select up to two of the six suggested distractors, and to write at least one distractor by themselves such that there is a total of three.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: The task was advertised on Amazon Mechanical Turk , requiring Master’s status for the crowdworkers

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: A person was presented with an original science exam question and a crowdsourced question. The instructions were to choose which of the two questions was more likely to be the real exam question. ... People identified the science exam question in 55% of the cases

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: requiring Master’s status for the crowdworkers

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: we use a model trained on real science exam questions to predict good answer distractors given a question and a correct answer. ... As classifier we chose a random forest

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Because the multiple choice question is trivial to answer when given the correct passage, the multiple choice version of SciQ does not include the passage... A small percentage of the passages were obtained from unreleasable texts, so the direct answer version of SciQ is slightly smaller

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We randomly shuffled this dataset and split it into training, validation and test portions... We also show that using SciQ as an additional source of training data improves performance on real 4th and 8th grade exam questions
